status: curated 2026-09-07 -- every entry cites a regulator fact sheet or a position stand. Adding an interaction means adding an entry WITH a source; an entry without a source is a model prior wearing a table's clothes and belongs in the model fill-in instead.

policy.scope: Interactions between actives that can appear together on ONE label, and notes about a specific form or salt. Drug interactions are out of scope: this reads a label, not a medicine cabinet.
policy.severity: info = worth knowing, no action; moderate = timing or dose matters at label-typical doses; high = documented risk at doses this product could deliver.
policy.matching: Aliases are matched as whole words on the normalised printed name. An active that matches no alias is passed to the model fill-in and shown as model knowledge, never as curated.

interactions.advice: Take the iron and the calcium at different times of day.
interactions.mechanism: Calcium taken with iron reduces absorption of both heme and non-heme iron in single-meal studies; the effect is smaller over whole diets, so separation matters most for a supplement dose.

source.title: NIH ODS — Iron, Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

interactions.advice: Taking them together helps: vitamin C improves non-heme iron absorption.
interactions.mechanism: Ascorbic acid reduces ferric to ferrous iron and forms a soluble chelate, increasing non-heme iron absorption.

source.title: NIH ODS — Iron, Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

interactions.advice: Long-term zinc at or above 50 mg/day can induce copper deficiency; check the total zinc across everything you take.
interactions.mechanism: High zinc intake up-regulates intestinal metallothionein, which binds copper and blocks its absorption; sustained intakes of 50 mg/day and above have produced copper deficiency.

source.title: NIH ODS — Zinc, Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

interactions.advice: High-dose iron taken without food can lower zinc absorption; taking both with a meal or hours apart avoids it.
interactions.mechanism: Iron at supplemental doses (about 25 mg and above) taken in solution without food reduces zinc absorption; the effect is not seen when taken with a meal.

source.title: NIH ODS — Zinc, Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

interactions.advice: Only very high zinc doses interfere with magnesium absorption; label-typical zinc does not.
interactions.mechanism: Zinc at 142 mg/day interfered with magnesium absorption and balance in a controlled study; ordinary supplemental zinc has not shown this.

source.title: NIH ODS — Magnesium, Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

interactions.advice: High-dose vitamin E can work against vitamin K; relevant if you take anticoagulants or the vitamin E dose is far above the RDA.
interactions.mechanism: Vitamin E at high doses inhibits vitamin K-dependent carboxylation and can potentiate anticoagulant effects, increasing bleeding risk.

source.title: NIH ODS — Vitamin E, Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

interactions.advice: High folic acid intake can hide a vitamin B12 deficiency by correcting the anaemia while nerve damage continues; the pairing on one label is fine, the concern is folic acid alone at high doses.
interactions.mechanism: Folic acid corrects megaloblastic anaemia regardless of cause, masking the haematological sign of B12 deficiency while neurological damage progresses.

source.title: NIH ODS — Folate, Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

interactions.advice: A sensible pairing: vitamin D is needed to absorb calcium in the gut.
interactions.mechanism: 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D increases intestinal calcium absorption; without adequate vitamin D only 10-15% of dietary calcium is absorbed.

source.title: NIH ODS — Vitamin D, Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

interactions.advice: Piperine is added to raise curcumin's otherwise very low oral bioavailability.
interactions.mechanism: Piperine inhibits hepatic and intestinal glucuronidation of curcumin, raising plasma curcumin severalfold in human pharmacokinetic studies.

source.title: Shoba G et al. Influence of piperine on the pharmacokinetics of curcumin in animals and human volunteers. Planta Med 1998

form_notes.note: Magnesium oxide is absorbed less completely than the citrate, chloride, lactate and aspartate forms; a high printed mg figure overstates what is absorbed.

source.title: NIH ODS — Magnesium, Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

form_notes.note: Citrate is among the better-absorbed magnesium forms; it also has a laxative effect at higher doses.

source.title: NIH ODS — Magnesium, Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

form_notes.note: Chloride is among the better-absorbed magnesium forms; note that its hydration state is often unstated, which makes the elemental dose ambiguous.

source.title: NIH ODS — Magnesium, Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

form_notes.note: Monohydrate is the form used in the large majority of trials and the reference against which other creatine forms are compared; no other form has shown superior uptake or effect.

source.title: Kreider RB et al. ISSN position stand: safety and efficacy of creatine supplementation. JISSN 2017;14:18

form_notes.note: Buffered creatine has not shown greater muscle creatine retention or performance benefit than monohydrate at equal doses.

source.title: Kreider RB et al. ISSN position stand: safety and efficacy of creatine supplementation. JISSN 2017;14:18

form_notes.note: Both D2 and D3 raise serum 25(OH)D; at higher doses D3 appears to raise and sustain it more than D2.

source.title: NIH ODS — Vitamin D, Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

form_notes.note: Ferrous (Fe2+) salts are absorbed better than ferric (Fe3+) forms; the elemental iron per tablet differs several-fold between salts, so compare elemental amounts, not compound mass.

source.title: NIH ODS — Iron, Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

form_notes.note: Zinc forms differ in elemental content and absorption; zinc oxide is poorly soluble and less well absorbed than gluconate, citrate or picolinate at equal elemental dose.

source.title: NIH ODS — Zinc, Fact Sheet for Health Professionals
